summary: In a feature branch workflow, every change goes on its own branch, gets pushed and reviewed, and is merged into main. Then everyone pulls main.
notes: On GitHub, the review and merge happen in a pull request: it shows the branch's diff, collects comments, and has a Merge button that does what Jordan's merge and push do here.
--no-ff makes a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible, which is what GitHub's default merge button does. It records that the feature came in as one unit.
Keep main working at all times. Unfinished work lives on branches until it is reviewed.
pitfall: Starting a new branch from an old main leads to conflicts later. Run git switch main and git pull before git switch -c.
setup_note: Starts in Maya's clone of ../gradebook.git, on main. Her teammate Jordan has his own clone in ../jordan.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
